[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance defines guardrails and convergence controls for AI agent review-fix loops — whether triggered by automation (timer-based workflows, event-driven pipelines) or initiated by humans (manually invoking `@copilot`, requesting an agent fix, or iterating through a review conversation). When an AI reviewer agent and an AI fix agent operate in a feedback loop — whether in pull requests, document reviews, design validation, or any iterative correction cycle — unbounded iteration can occur if the system lacks mechanisms to distinguish actionable findings from subjective feedback and to recognize when convergence has been achieved. The convergence failure modes are identical regardless of whether a human or a scheduler initiates each cycle.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Reduced compute waste**: Prevents runaway agent iterations that consume LLM inference tokens without proportional value
- **Predictable completion**: Teams can rely on review-fix loops completing in bounded iterations regardless of the review domain or trigger mechanism (human or automated)
- **Appropriate human escalation**: Subjective, ambiguous, or architectural issues route to human judgment rather than producing infinite agent churn
- **Model cost governance**: Explicit model declaration and iteration caps control LLM token spend across all agent interactions

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#applicable-scenarios]

#### Applicable Scenarios

- **Code review loops**: AI reviewer (e.g., GitHub Copilot Pull Request Reviewer) + AI fix agent (e.g., GitHub Copilot coding agent) iterating on pull requests — triggered by automation (scheduled workflow) or by a human (`@copilot` mention)
- **Document review loops**: AI reviewer evaluating documentation quality + AI author agent correcting findings — triggered by CI or by human request
- **Design validation loops**: AI architecture reviewer + AI design agent iterating on design artifacts
- **Any feedback cycle** where one AI agent produces findings and another AI agent attempts to resolve them iteratively, regardless of what triggers each iteration (human, timer, event, or webhook)

#### Business Drivers

- **AI-assisted workflow acceleration**: Organizations are adopting AI agent pairs (reviewer + fixer) to automate iterative quality improvement across code, documentation, and design artifacts
- **Cost control**: LLM inference is not free — unbounded iteration multiplies token consumption without proportional value

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#current-state-assessment]

#### Current State Assessment

AI reviewer agents generate findings (comments, annotations, or structured feedback). AI fix agents consume those findings and attempt corrections. This pattern appears across multiple domains:

- **Code**: Reviewer comments on PRs → fix agent pushes code changes → re-review
- **Documentation**: Reviewer flags quality issues → author agent rewrites → re-review
- **Design**: Validator flags constraint violations → design agent adjusts → re-validate

Without guardrails, all of these loops exhibit the same failure modes:

- The fix agent addresses all findings equally — subjective suggestions, scope-expanding requests, and genuine defects
- Fixing a peripheral issue can introduce new review surface (new files, new terminology, new dependencies) triggering additional findings
- The reviewer re-evaluates after each correction, potentially finding new issues introduced by the fix or re-raising resolved issues
- No mechanism exists to signal "good enough" — the loop runs until a hard cap is hit or a human intervenes
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#future-state-vision]

#### Future State Vision

A well-governed review-fix loop that:

1. Converges in 1–3 iterations for artifacts with only routine findings
2. Self-terminates when no objectively actionable findings remain
3. Escalates subjective and architectural issues to human judgment
4. Declares its model and iteration budget explicitly for auditability
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#problem-description]

#### Problem Description

Without convergence guardrails, an AI review-fix loop can iterate 9+ times on a single artifact without reaching a stable state — regardless of whether each iteration is triggered by a timer, an event, or a human typing `@copilot fix this`. Root causes:

1. **No finding triage**: The fix agent treats every reviewer finding as equally actionable, including subjective suggestions, scope-expanding requests, and architectural questions
2. **Blast radius expansion**: Addressing peripheral findings (documentation, naming, structure) touches artifacts outside the original scope, creating new review surface
3. **Stale finding blindness**: The loop re-processes findings that have already been addressed by prior corrections (the reviewer may mark them resolved, but the loop doesn't check)
4. **No exit condition**: The agent has no instruction to stop when only subjective or out-of-scope findings remain
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#impact-assessment]

#### Impact Assessment

- **Compute cost**: Each iteration invokes LLM inference for both review and fix — 9 iterations at ~$0.50–$2.00 per invocation = $4.50–$18.00 per artifact (scales with team size and artifact count)
- **Delivery delay**: Each iteration adds 5–15 minutes of wall-clock time; 9 iterations = 45–135 minutes of blocked delivery
- **Noise**: Repeated findings clutter artifact history, making human review harder when escalation eventually occurs
- **Trust erosion**: Teams lose confidence in AI automation when it visibly churns without converging

### Success Criteria

| Success Area | Metrics | Measurement Approach | Target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Convergence Speed | Iterations to stable state | Count fix-request cycles per artifact | ≤ 3 iterations |
| Self-Termination | % of loops where agent correctly stops | Monitor "no actionable findings" replies | > 80% of applicable loops |
| Cost Efficiency | LLM spend per loop | Token usage tracking | < $5.00 per review-fix loop |
| Human Escalation | Subjective issues routed to humans | Audit deferred findings | 100% of non-objective issues |

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#principle-1-triage-before-fix]

#### Principle 1: Triage Before Fix

**Description:** The fix agent must classify each reviewer finding before acting on it. Only concrete, objectively verifiable findings warrant correction — whether the fix is dispatched by automation or requested by a human.

**Rationale:** Subjective findings (terminology preferences, stylistic suggestions, architectural questions) cannot be resolved by mechanical changes alone and create divergent iteration paths.

**Application:** The fix prompt must explicitly instruct the agent to categorize findings into "actionable" (objective, verifiable) and "defer" (subjective, scope-expanding, architectural). Only actionable findings are addressed.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#principle-2-scope-lock]

#### Principle 2: Scope Lock

**Description:** The fix agent must only modify artifacts within its declared scope. Artifacts outside the declared boundary are off-limits regardless of what the reviewer suggests.

**Rationale:** Modifying artifacts outside the original scope expands the blast radius, creating new review surface that triggers additional findings in an unbounded expansion loop.

**Application:** The fix prompt must declare allowed artifact boundaries (e.g., source code and tests but not documentation; or a specific document but not its referenced diagrams) and explicitly forbid modification outside those boundaries.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#principle-3-bounded-iteration]

#### Principle 3: Bounded Iteration

**Description:** Every review-fix loop must declare a maximum iteration count. When reached, the loop stops and escalates to a human reviewer.

**Rationale:** Even with triage and scope lock, edge cases can cause continued iteration. A hard cap guarantees termination.

**Application:** Configure the loop workflow with a `MAX_ITERATIONS` constant (recommended: 5) and post a human-escalation notice when reached.
page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#principle-4-explicit-model-declaration]

#### Principle 4: Explicit Model Declaration

**Description:** Every agent in the loop must declare its LLM model explicitly, not rely on platform defaults.

**Rationale:** Platform defaults change without notice. Explicit declaration enables cost forecasting, A/B testing, and reproducible behavior audits. When convergence issues occur, knowing which model was used is essential for diagnosis.

**Application:** Set the model identifier in the agent's configuration (e.g., `model:` field in `gh-aw` engine blocks, model parameter in API calls, or equivalent platform-specific configuration).
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#principle-5-stale-finding-awareness]

#### Principle 5: Stale Finding Awareness

**Description:** The loop must detect and skip findings that have been superseded by subsequent corrections.

**Rationale:** After a correction is applied, the reviewer's earlier findings may no longer apply (the code has changed, the paragraph was rewritten, the design was restructured). Re-processing stale findings leads to redundant or impossible corrections.

**Application:** Before dispatching a fix request, check whether prior findings still apply to the current state of the artifact. In code review contexts, filter comments where `position === null`. In document contexts, compare finding locations against the current revision.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#approach-1-triage-aware-fix-prompt]

#### Approach 1: Triage-Aware Fix Prompt

**Overview:** Design the fix-request prompt to include explicit triage instructions that tell the fix agent what to address and what to skip.

**When to Use:** Any review-fix loop — automated or human-initiated — where the fix agent receives reviewer findings.

**Implementation (code review example):**

```markdown
@copilot Review the unresolved review comments on this PR. For each comment:
- If it identifies a **concrete code defect** (unused import, type error, missing export, logic bug): fix it.
- If it is a documentation terminology suggestion, architectural question, or style preference: **skip it**.

**Rules:**
- Only modify files under `components/` and `tests/`.
- Do NOT modify any `.md` files in `docs/`.
- Do NOT rename public types or restructure layer definitions.
- Push a single commit addressing only concrete code defects.
- If there are no concrete code defects to fix, reply with:
  "No actionable code defects remain — deferring to human review."
```

**Implementation (generalized pattern):**

```markdown
Review the outstanding findings. For each finding:
- If it identifies an **objectively verifiable defect** within the declared scope: fix it.
- If it is subjective, scope-expanding, or requires human judgment: **skip it**.

If no actionable findings remain, reply:
"No actionable findings remain — deferring to human review."
```

**Benefits:** Agent self-terminates when only subjective issues remain; reduces iterations from 9+ to 1–3.

**Considerations:** The prompt must be maintained as agent capabilities evolve. Test with representative artifacts before deploying broadly.
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#approach-2-pre-submission-checklist-for-fix-agents]

#### Approach 2: Pre-Submission Checklist for Fix Agents

**Overview:** Equip the fix agent (via its `.agent.md` instructions) with a checklist of common defects to proactively verify before submitting, reducing the reviewer's comment surface on first pass.

**When to Use:** When the same categories of defects recur across PRs (unused imports, untyped parameters, bare generics).

**Implementation:** Add a "Pre-submission Checklist" section to the agent's instruction file:

```markdown
## Pre-submission Checklist (verify before creating the PR)

- All imports are used — run `ruff check --select F401` and fix violations
- All public types use explicit generic type parameters
- All public functions have fully-typed parameters and return types
- Terminology in docstrings matches the project glossary
- Do NOT modify documentation files outside feature scope
```

**Benefits:** Reduces first-pass reviewer comments, shortening the loop from the start.

**Considerations:** Keep the checklist focused on objectively verifiable items. Subjective style rules should not be in the checklist.
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#approach-3-stale-finding-filtering]

#### Approach 3: Stale Finding Filtering

**Overview:** Before dispatching a fix request, the loop checks whether prior findings still apply to the current state of the artifact. Findings that have been superseded by corrections are filtered out.

**When to Use:** Any review-fix loop where the reviewer's findings reference specific locations that may shift after corrections.

**Implementation (GitHub PR example):**

```javascript
const activeComments = reviewComments.data.filter(c =>
  c.user.login === 'copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]' &&
  c.position !== null &&
  new Date(c.created_at).getTime() >= latestReviewTime - 60000
);

if (activeComments.length === 0) {
  console.log('All findings outdated — artifact is converging');
  continue; // skip fix request
}
```

**Implementation (generalized pattern):**

- Compare each finding's referenced location (line, paragraph, section) against the current artifact revision
- If the location no longer exists or the content has changed, mark the finding as stale
- Only dispatch fix requests when at least one finding is still active

**Benefits:** Prevents re-processing findings that were addressed by a previous correction.

**Considerations:** A small time window (e.g., 60 seconds) accounts for clock skew between finding creation and correction timestamps.
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#best-practice-1-declare-model-explicitly]

#### Best Practice 1: Declare Model Explicitly

**Description:** Set `model: <model-name>` in the `engine:` block of every agentic workflow file.

**Rationale:** Platform defaults change. Explicit declaration enables version pinning, cost auditing, and A/B comparisons.

**Implementation:**

```yaml
engine:
  id: copilot
  model: claude-sonnet-4
  agent: implementation-agent
```

**Success Indicators:** All workflow files contain a `model:` field; no workflow relies on implicit defaults.
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#best-practice-2-cap-iterations-at-5]

#### Best Practice 2: Cap Iterations at 5

**Description:** Set a maximum iteration count (recommended: 5) for the review-fix loop. Post a human-escalation notice when the cap is reached.

**Rationale:** Based on empirical observation, loops that cannot converge in 5 iterations contain issues that require human judgment (architectural concerns, subjective style, scope changes).

**Implementation:** Track fix-request cycles by marker or counter. Stop at the cap and notify human stakeholders.

**Success Indicators:** No loop exceeds 5 fix iterations (whether human-triggered or automated); escalation notices appear in the interaction history.
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#best-practice-3-scope-lock-the-fix-agent]

#### Best Practice 3: Scope-Lock the Fix Agent

**Description:** The fix prompt must explicitly declare which artifacts the fix agent may modify and which are off-limits.

**Rationale:** Prevents blast radius expansion when the agent modifies artifacts outside the original scope.

**Implementation:** Declare boundaries explicitly (e.g., "Only modify source code and tests" or "Only modify the specified document section"). List forbidden artifact types.

**Success Indicators:** Fix corrections touch only in-scope artifacts; no unintended scope expansion.
page_texts.37:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#pitfall-1-treating-all-findings-as-equally-actionable]

#### Pitfall 1: Treating All Findings as Equally Actionable

**Description:** The fix agent attempts to resolve every reviewer finding regardless of category — including subjective suggestions, scope-expanding requests, and architectural questions.

**Impact:** Each peripheral fix creates new review surface. The loop diverges instead of converging. 9+ iterations observed in practice.

**Prevention:** Include explicit triage instructions in the fix prompt. Categorize findings and skip non-actionable categories.

**Mitigation:** If already in a divergent state, inject a manual stop signal and reset the loop.
page_texts.38:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#pitfall-2-no-exit-condition-for-subjective-findings]

#### Pitfall 2: No Exit Condition for Subjective Findings

**Description:** The agent has no instruction to stop when only subjective findings remain. It attempts to "fix" style or terminology findings by modifying artifacts, which triggers new review findings.

**Impact:** Infinite loop until iteration cap is hit.

**Prevention:** Include an explicit exit instruction: "If there are no objectively actionable findings to fix, reply with 'No actionable findings remain' and do NOT make changes."

**Mitigation:** Increase the fix prompt's triage specificity; add the exit condition instruction.
page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#pitfall-3-implicit-model-defaults]

#### Pitfall 3: Implicit Model Defaults

**Description:** Relying on platform-default model selection without declaring it in the workflow configuration.

**Impact:** Model changes (upgrades or downgrades) happen silently, causing unpredictable behavior changes and cost spikes. Debugging convergence issues is harder without knowing which model was used.

**Prevention:** Always set `model:` in the engine block. Document the rationale for model selection.

**Mitigation:** Audit existing workflows for missing `model:` fields; add explicit declarations retroactively.
page_texts.40:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#pitfall-4-re-processing-stale-findings]

#### Pitfall 4: Re-Processing Stale Findings

**Description:** The loop processes all reviewer findings including those already addressed by prior corrections. The findings reference locations or content that no longer exists in the current artifact state.

**Impact:** The agent attempts fixes for issues that no longer exist, producing spurious changes or confusion messages.

**Prevention:** Check whether each finding still applies to the current artifact state before dispatching fix requests. Filter by location validity, revision timestamp, or resolution status.

**Mitigation:** Add stale-finding detection to the loop and redeploy.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#methodology-overview]

#### Methodology Overview

Adopt convergence guardrails incrementally: start with the fix prompt triage (highest impact, lowest effort), then add comment filtering, iteration caps, and finally explicit model governance.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#phase-1-triage-aware-fix-prompt]

#### Phase 1: Triage-Aware Fix Prompt

**Objectives:** Eliminate the primary cause of divergence — the agent treating all findings equally.

**Key Activities:**

1. Update the fix-request prompt in the loop orchestrator
2. Add explicit categorization instructions (fix objective findings, skip subjective ones)
3. Add scope-lock rules (allowed artifacts, forbidden artifacts)
4. Add exit condition ("no actionable findings remain")

**Deliverables:** Updated fix prompt template in the orchestrator configuration

**Success Criteria:** Next 3 agent-processed loops converge in ≤ 3 iterations.
page_texts.50:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#phase-2-stale-finding-filtering]

#### Phase 2: Stale Finding Filtering

**Objectives:** Prevent re-processing of already-addressed findings.

**Key Activities:**

1. Add logic to check whether findings still apply to the current artifact state
2. Add time-window or revision check to isolate findings from the latest review cycle
3. Skip fix dispatch when all active findings are stale

**Deliverables:** Updated loop orchestrator with stale-finding detection

**Success Criteria:** Zero fix requests dispatched for stale-only finding sets.
page_texts.51:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#phase-3-model-and-budget-governance]

#### Phase 3: Model and Budget Governance

**Objectives:** Make model selection and iteration budget explicit and auditable.

**Key Activities:**

1. Add explicit model declaration to all agent configurations
2. Set `MAX_ITERATIONS` constant (recommended: 5)
3. Add human-escalation notice when cap is reached
4. Update any compiled/generated artifacts

**Deliverables:** Updated agent configurations with explicit model and iteration budget

**Success Criteria:** All agent interactions declare model explicitly; no loop exceeds iteration cap without escalation.
page_texts.52:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#phase-4-pre-submission-checklist]

#### Phase 4: Pre-Submission Checklist

**Objectives:** Reduce first-pass reviewer findings by catching common issues before the artifact is submitted for review.

**Key Activities:**

1. Analyze the most common reviewer findings across recent loops
2. Distill into an objectively verifiable checklist
3. Add checklist to the fix agent's instruction file or configuration
4. Validate that agent output improves on next iteration

**Deliverables:** Updated agent instruction files with pre-submission validation

**Success Criteria:** First-pass reviewer finding count decreases by > 50%.
page_texts.54:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#critical-success-factor-1-prompt-precision]

#### Critical Success Factor 1: Prompt Precision

**Description:** The triage instructions in the fix prompt must be specific enough that the agent can reliably categorize findings.

**Importance:** Vague instructions like "fix important issues" leave the agent to guess, reverting to the treat-everything-equally behavior.

**Implementation:** Use concrete examples in the prompt — name specific actionable finding types (unused import, type error, broken link, invalid constraint) and specific skip categories (style preference, terminology choice, architectural question).

**Measurement:** Audit fix corrections for scope violations (artifacts outside allowed boundaries, unintended changes).
page_texts.55:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#critical-success-factor-2-team-alignment-on-finding-categories]

#### Critical Success Factor 2: Team Alignment on Finding Categories

**Description:** The team must agree on what constitutes an objectively actionable finding vs. a subjective suggestion.

**Importance:** If the reviewer generates findings that the fix agent correctly skips but the team considers mandatory, the loop appears broken.

**Implementation:** Document the categorization in the project's agent configuration (AGENTS.md, contributing guide, or equivalent). Review with the team before deploying.

**Measurement:** Zero disputes about whether the agent "should have" fixed a skipped finding.
page_texts.58:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#decision-point-1-which-model-to-use]

#### Decision Point 1: Which Model to Use

**Context:** When configuring a new agentic workflow or updating an existing one.

**Options:**

| Model | Strengths | Cost | Recommended For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-sonnet-4` | Fast, cost-effective, good at routine code tasks | Lower | Implementation, testing, documentation agents |
| `claude-opus-4` | Higher reasoning capability, better at complex refactoring | Higher | Complex architectural changes, multi-file refactors |
| `gpt-4o` | Good general-purpose, fast | Medium | General-purpose fallback |

**Criteria:** Default to `claude-sonnet-4` for routine agent tasks. Upgrade to `claude-opus-4` only if convergence doesn't improve after implementing all other guardrails.

**Recommendation:** Start with `claude-sonnet-4` across all agents. Observe convergence metrics for 2 weeks. Upgrade individual workflows only where convergence remains problematic.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-008-ai-agent-review-loop-convergence-guidance.md#decision-point-2-iteration-cap-value]

#### Decision Point 2: Iteration Cap Value

**Context:** Choosing the `MAX_ITERATIONS` value for the review loop.

**Options:**

| Value | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| 3 | Aggressive — may escalate PRs that would have converged in 4 iterations |
| 5 | Balanced — covers most converging PRs while bounding cost |
| 10 | Permissive — allows more agent autonomy but higher cost and delay |

**Criteria:** Analyze historical iteration counts. If > 90% of converging PRs complete within N iterations, set cap to N+1.

**Recommendation:** Start at 5. Reduce to 3 after confirming that guardrails achieve consistent convergence.

### Real-World Example: Code Review Loop (eap-golden-path-poc)

**Context:** A polyglot enterprise template repository using GitHub Copilot Pull Request Reviewer (AI reviewer) + GitHub Copilot coding agent (AI fix agent) in a review-fix loop. The loop operates in two modes: (1) automated via a timer-based workflow that polls for outstanding reviews, and (2) human-initiated via `@copilot` mentions on PR comments. Both modes exhibited identical convergence failures before guardrails were applied.

**Challenge:** PRs iterated 9+ times without converging. The fix agent modified documentation files in response to terminology comments, which expanded the review surface. The reviewer found new issues in the modified docs, and the cycle continued.

**Application:**

1. Added triage-aware fix prompt — agent now skips documentation/terminology/style findings
2. Added scope lock — agent can only modify `components/` and `tests/`
3. Added stale finding filter — skips findings where `position === null`
4. Added pre-submission checklist — catches unused imports, bare generics, untyped functions before PR creation
5. Added explicit `model: claude-sonnet-4` to all 5 workflow engine blocks

**Outcomes:** Expected convergence in 1–3 iterations (monitoring in progress). Clear audit trail of which model processed each loop.

**Lessons Learned:**

- The fix prompt is the highest-leverage intervention — a single paragraph of triage instructions eliminated the primary divergence cause
- Scope lock is essential even with good triage — prevents accidental blast radius expansion
- Model declaration costs nothing but enables future debugging and cost attribution
- These principles apply identically to non-code review loops (documentation, design artifacts) — the divergence mechanics are the same

#### Governance Structure

- **Ownership**: Platform Engineering owns loop orchestrator configuration; individual teams own their agent instruction files
- **Review cadence**: Quarterly audit of convergence metrics and prompt effectiveness
- **Exception handling**: Teams may request iteration cap increases via ADR with cost justification
- **Model changes**: Model upgrades require a test run on 3 representative artifacts before fleet-wide rollout

#### Risk Assessment

| Risk Category | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Divergence recurrence | New comment categories emerge that the triage prompt doesn't handle | Medium | Medium | Quarterly prompt review based on escalated PRs |
| Model regression | Platform model update degrades convergence | Low | High | Explicit model pinning; test before adopting new versions |
| Over-suppression | Triage skips genuine defects | Low | Medium | Audit skipped comments monthly; refine triage categories |
| Cost overrun | Loop runs at cap on many PRs | Low | Medium | Monitor iteration histograms; lower cap if > 10% hit limit |

#### Assessment Dimensions

- **Convergence**: Does the loop terminate in bounded iterations?
- **Correctness**: Does the agent fix objective findings and skip subjective ones?
- **Cost**: Is the per-loop LLM spend within budget?
- **Escalation quality**: Are escalated artifacts genuinely beyond agent capability?
